amendments.body: Fix failing test `plant_limitation_is_tank_size_independent` in `crates/tank_core/tests/plant_nutrient_normalization.rs:75-115`. The test expects 1e-9 tolerance between 10L and 100L tanks (same 50×20cm footprint), but Beer-Lambert light attenuation is now depth-dependent: 10L→10cm fill vs 100L→100cm fill produces legitimately different light factors via `column_average_attenuation_factor(k, h)`. Either adjust the test to use different footprints so both tanks have the same water depth, or separate the assertion into nutrient-limitation-only checks (which are volume-independent) and a light-factor check (which is correctly depth-dependent).
amendments.rationale: This is a hard test failure in the acceptance criteria's own tank-size-independence test. The Beer-Lambert attenuation added in this PR makes light physically depth-dependent, which is correct science but contradicts the test's assumption that all limitation factors are volume-independent at constant concentration. The test must be reconciled with the new physics.

amendments.body: Fix failing test `nitrification_lowers_alkalinity_and_ph` in `crates/tank_core/tests/chemistry.rs:188`. The nitrogen-cycle Ks default values changed dramatically in this PR (e.g., AOB K_s(TAN) effectively went from 0.025 mg/L to 1.0 mg/L — a 40× increase). With 2.0 mg/L TAN, the Monod factor dropped from ~0.99 to ~0.67, significantly slowing nitrification. The test's 48-hour window is no longer sufficient for pH separation. Either increase the simulation duration, increase nitrifier biomass, or adjust the TAN concentration to produce enough nitrification activity under the new parameters.
amendments.rationale: This is a hard test failure. The parameter value changes are scientifically motivated (literature-range values) but the chemistry integration test was not updated to account for the slower kinetics.

amendments.body: Fix wrong serde alias on `ProcessParamsPreset::aob_k_tan_mg_n_per_l` in `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:774`. Current alias is `"aob_k_tan_mg_n_per_l"` (identical to the field name — a no-op). It should be `"aob_k_tan_mg"` to accept the legacy TOML field name, matching the pattern used by all other renamed fields (e.g., `aob_k_do_mg_per_l` correctly aliases `"aob_k_do_mg"`, `nob_k_nitrite_mg_n_per_l` correctly aliases `"nob_k_nitrite_mg"`, etc.).
amendments.rationale: Any custom TOML preset file that still uses the old field name `aob_k_tan_mg` will silently fall back to the default value instead of deserializing the user's tuned value. This is a silent data-loss bug for anyone with custom process parameter presets.

amendments.body: Evaluate the safety of removing `reconcile_egg_cohort_counts()` from `enforce_invariants` (crates/tank_core/src/invariants.rs:42 removed, :183-192 added strict validation). The old code auto-repaired mismatches between `berried_females_count` and `egg_cohort_count_total()` every tick. The new code returns `SimError::InvariantViolation` if they differ. The save/load path calls `repair_egg_cohort_counts_for_load`, but during live simulation, any edge case that creates a transient mismatch (e.g., a race between mortality clamping and egg resolution) will now crash the engine instead of self-healing. Consider either keeping the repair in enforce_invariants (with the strict check in validate only), or adding an explicit assertion that the shrimp system always maintains the invariant before enforce_invariants runs.
amendments.rationale: Converting a self-healing repair to a hard error is a robustness risk. The shrimp code appears to maintain the invariant carefully, but the old reconcile was a safety net. If any code path is missed, this becomes a runtime crash in production instead of a silent fix.

payload.summary: Reviewed the plant nutrient normalization changes (tanksim-6e5.2.4). The core refactoring is well-structured: parameter renames from legacy total-mass to concentration-based semantics are correct, Beer-Lambert light attenuation physics is sound, migration chain (v7→v10) properly converts saved values, and unit tests for individual limitation terms are thorough. However, there are two hard test failures (`plant_limitation_is_tank_size_independent` due to Beer-Lambert depth dependence conflicting with the volume-independence assumption, and `nitrification_lowers_alkalinity_and_ph` due to dramatically changed Ks defaults), one wrong serde alias in presets.rs that silently drops user-tuned AOB TAN Ks values, and a robustness concern from replacing the egg-cohort auto-repair with a strict invariant error.
